sections.text_helper: Section 52.4.6 "Modular exponentiation" in chapter 52 (Public key accelerator (PKA)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 2462.
sections.section_content:
Modular exponentiation operation is commonly used to perform a single-step RSA
operation. It calculates of Aemodn.
RSA operation involving public information (RSA encryption) can use the normal or fast
mode detailed on Table448 and Table449. RSA operation involving secret information
(RSA decryption) must use the protected mode detailed on Table450, for security reason.
Note: Once this operation is started PKA control register and PKA memory is no more available.
Access is restored once BUSY bit is set to 0 by the PKA.
When this operation completes with errors due to unexpected hardware events a PKA
tamper event is triggered to TAMP peripheral, and access to PKA RAM becomes blocked
until erased by hardware.
Note: When MODE[5:0]=0x03, the error code is not affected when PKA automatically clears the
PKA RAM at the end of this protected operation. When the error output equals 0xD60D, the
result output is not affected either.
Operation instructions for modular exponentiation are summarized in Table448 (normal
mode), Table449 (fast mode), and Table450 (protected mode). Fast mode usage is
explained in Section52.3.6.
